{{Short description|American statistician}}

'''Lawrence I-Kuei Lin''' is an American statistician. 

Lin earned his doctorate from the [[University of Iowa]] in 1979, where, advised by [[Peter A. Lachenbruch]], he authored the dissertation ''The Effect of Non-Normality on Multiple Group Discrimination and Estimation of the Logistic Risk Function when Data Are Heavy-Tailed with Clumping at Zero''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref>

Lin worked for [[Baxter Healthcare]] and is also an adjunct professor at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Special Lectures and Seminars October 20 |url=https://digitalcollections.lib.iastate.edu/islandora/object/isu%3AStatsAnnualReports_4278 |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=Iowa State University Library Digital Collections |date=1995}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Lin Adjunct Professor |url=https://www.math.uic.edu/persisting_utilities/people/profile?netid=equelilin |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=University of Illinois Chicago}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Lin |url=https://mscs.uic.edu/profiles/equelilin/ |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=University of Illinois Chicago}}</ref> He was elected a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=ASA Fellows |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=American Statistical Association}}</ref>
